questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence using exclamatory inversion with 'Here' or 'There':
options: There goes the bus.
There go the bus.
There is going the bus.
There went the bus.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence expressing a universal truth:
options: The Earth is revolving around the Sun.
The Earth revolved around the Sun.
The Earth revolves around the Sun.
The Earth will revolve around the Sun.

questions.question: Choose the correct Present Perfect Passive sentence:
options: The guests have entertained properly.
The guests have been entertained properly.
The guests are being entertained properly.
The guests were entertained properly.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct Indirect Narration sentence (Sequence of tenses):
options: I asked him why he is telling a lie.
I asked him why he was telling a lie.
I asked him why he told a lie.
I asked him why he is telling a lie.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct Indirect Narration sentence (Yes/No question):
options: The seller asked me that I wanted to buy shoes.
The seller asked me whether I wanted to buy shoes.
The seller asked me if I want to buy shoes.
The seller asked me whether I did want to buy shoes.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence using 'did not':
options: The students did not stood up when the teacher came.
The students did not stand up when the teacher came.
The students did not standing up when the teacher came.
The students did not stands up when the teacher came.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct interrogative sentence:
options: What does you want from me?
What do you want from me?
What you want from me?
What did you want from me?

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct interrogative sentence using 'did':
options: Where did the thief hid the stolen watch?
Where did the thief hide the stolen watch?
Where did the thief hidden the stolen watch?
Where did the thief hiding the stolen watch?

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct indirect exclamation:
options: He exclaimed that he is very unlucky.
He exclaimed that he was very unlucky.
He exclaimed that he was how unlucky.
He exclaimed that he is how unlucky.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence using the fixed preposition with 'invited':
options: I was invited on the party.
I was invited at the party.
I was invited to the party.
I was invited in the party.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct conditional/time-clause sentence:
options: When it will rain, farmers sow their fields.
When it rains, farmers sow their fields.
When it rained, farmers will sow their fields.
When it is raining, farmers sowed their fields.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence using 'had better':
options: You had better to study for the exam.
You had better studying for the exam.
You had better study for the exam.
You had better to studying for the exam.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct past interrogative sentence:
options: When did he saw the movie?
When did he see the movie?
When did he seen the movie?
When did he seeing the movie?

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct Present Perfect Continuous sentence:
options: He has been living here since 2010.
He has been lived here since 2010.
He is been living here since 2010.
He has living here since 2010.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct negative interrogative sentence:
options: Didn't you completed your homework?
Did you not complete your homework?
Didn't you complete your homework?
Don't you complete your homework?

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence using 'warn':
options: The instructor warned the driver not to drive fast.
The instructor warned the driver to not drive fast.
The instructor warned the driver not driving fast.
The instructor warned the driver that not to drive fast.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence involving backshifting with 'had':
options: They said that they had did their work.
They said that they had done their work.
They said that they have done their work.
They said that they had doing their work.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence following the 'past follows past' rule:
options: Vasu assured that they will win the match.
Vasu assured that they would win the match.
Vasu assured that they won the match.
Vasu assured that they winning the match.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence using 'request':
options: She requested him bringing a glass of water.
She requested him to bring a glass of water.
She requested him that bring a glass of water.
She requested him bring a glass of water.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence using 'tell':
options: They told him attend the class regularly.
They told him to attend the class regularly.
They told him attending the class regularly.
They told him that attend the class regularly.
